summary: Redwood SE and AE walked the Sentinel Labs team through architecture tradeoffs between Hosted and Dedicated modes focusing on runtime performance: KV cache behavior, batching, quantization, noisy neighbor isolation, and VPC/on-prem requirements. Agreed next steps to run a representative benchmark on Dedicated with sample traces and to share detailed security docs.
meeting_header:
Date: 2025-07-09 | Time: 15:00 PT | Duration: 52m
Attendees: Samira Patel (Redwood AE), Eric Huang (Redwood SE), Carlos Mendez (Sentinel CTO), Priya Rao (ML Infra), Ben Li (Security)
Recording: https://app.fireflies.ai/recordings/ff-20250709-8743
transcript:
[00:00] Samira: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call - we're Samira and Eric from Redwood.
[00:07] Carlos: Hey, Carlos here. Priya and Ben are on as well.
[00:12] Samira: Great. We've got about 50 minutes. Goal today is a deep dive on Dedicated vs Hosted, performance and isolation concerns, and the on-prem/VPC/security checklist.
[02:45] Eric: I can start on the runtime side. At a high level, hosted is multi-tenant — we do a lot of continuous batching and prefix caching to reduce cost. Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools so noisy neighbor risk is lower, and you get more predictable throughput.
[03:30] Priya: Quick question on KV cache — how much does dedicated help with cache warm-up? We care about conversational apps with long contexts.
[03:45] Eric: Good question. Our KV cache (sometimes transcribed it as "kay vee" in old notes) is per-model and can be per-tenant on Dedicated. On Hosted, the cache is shared across warm flows but can't be pinned to a single customer instance, so you can see more cold-starts under certain traffic patterns. Dedicated lets you pin the cache so prefix hits are much higher for steady-state sessions.
[05:12] Carlos: What's the warm-up time? If a user's convo resumes after 10 minutes, do we lose the cache?
[05:20] Eric: It depends on memory and sequence length. For a 16k sequence model on H100, hot cache of recent keys is typically immediate for active sessions; idle eviction windows are configurable for Dedicated. On Hosted, eviction is shorter under pressure. Typical warm-up latency for a cold KV (full refill) is a few tokens' worth of extra compute — in practice worst-case maybe 20-40ms extra per token for the first few steps, but overall end-to-end p95 can jump if you trigger many cold contexts simultaneously.
[07:02] Priya: Are there options to pre-warm or pin prefixes?
[07:10] Eric: Yes. We support pre-warm calls and prefix caching APIs, and on Dedicated you can persist KV snapshots to speed restarts. We also offer sticky routing so long-lived sessions hit the same pool.
[09:30] Ben: From security: on Dedicated, do we get a private VPC and dedicated control plane? How is networking isolated?
[09:42] Samira: For Redwood Dedicated and Redwood Private we offer VPC peering, customer-managed subnets, and in Private deployments you can run the control plane inside your VPC. We'll share the VPC diagram and the KMS/HSM integration guide — Eric can point to the docs.
[10:18] Eric: One nuance: Dedicated gives you isolation at the GPU pool level, but the control plane and autoscaler may still talk to our managed services unless you choose the Private on-prem package. If you need full air-gap, Private is the way.
[11:05] Carlos: What about noisy neighbor within a dedicated pool — if we reserve a pool but multiple tenants of our own org run jobs, can one tenant spike and impact others?
[11:20] Eric: Within a single Dedicated pool, we provide tenant-aware scheduling. If you want absolute isolation you can reserve multiple pools per team. Also we expose QoS controls and per-route quotas so you can limit tail latency impact.
[12:55] Priya: Throughput guarantees — can you commit to a specific QPS and latency SLO for POCs?
[13:05] Samira: For Dedicated, we can produce capacity planning and commit to throughput with reserved capacity contracts. For Hosted it's best-effort with soft guarantees; we publish performance profiles but SLAs are stronger on Dedicated. We'll produce a recommended config based on your peak QPS and sequence lengths.
[14:30] Eric: Regarding batching: our runtime uses continuous batching which groups inflight requests up to a latency budget. On Hosted, batching is optimized across tenants which improves utilization but adds variance. On Dedicated, you control batching windows and latency budgets per pool, so you can trade higher throughput for slightly higher p95.
[15:05] Carlos: How deterministic is the batching behavior? We need tight p95 latency for interactive users.
[15:20] Eric: You can set a target latency (e.g., 50ms) and the system will flush batches at that boundary. For strict latency we recommend small batch sizes and higher reserved GPU count to keep utilization. We'll show p50/p95 curves for different batch targets.
[17:10] Priya: Quantization question — do you support 8-bit and 4-bit models in production? Any accuracy hits we should expect?
[17:22] Eric: Yes, we support int8 and 4-bit (GPTQ-style) quantizations. On a lot of open models 8-bit is near-lossless; 4-bit can introduce small regressions depending on the model and prompt. We include quality monitoring so you can run eval sets and roll back if you see regressions. Quantization reduces memory footprint and increases throughput, which is helpful for Dedicated when you want to squeeze more tokens per GPU.
[19:00] Carlos: Do quantized models affect KV cache behavior?
[19:08] Eric: Not directly. The KV cache is a runtime construct; quantization affects compute kernel speed and memory, which indirectly changes throughput and batch sizing. You might observe that quantized models allow more concurrent batches, changing cache pressure patterns.
[20:41] Samira: Another practical tradeoff — cost. Hosted is simpler and cheaper at low-to-medium scale because we multiplex across customers. Dedicated makes sense when you have predictable high QPS or strict data residency/compliance needs.
[21:10] Priya: For on-prem, what's the recommended HW? We have an on-prem data center with A100s and H100s.
[21:25] Eric: H100 is best for throughput and attention kernels; A100 is still solid. For 16k token contexts and high concurrency, we recommend H100s with NVLink if possible. We'll include a HW sizing doc.
[22:42] Ben: About auditing — do you provide audit logs and per-request attribution for Private?
[22:50] Samira: Yes, Private includes full audit logs, request tracing, and can integrate with SIEM. We'll send the audit log retention options and sample schema.
[24:30] Carlos: How does the runtime choose kernels — is that static or dynamic per workload?
[24:40] Eric: Dynamic. We do kernel selection at load time and also have runtime adaptors that pick optimal kernels based on sequence length and batch size. There is a compilation stage for custom kernels in Dedicated/Private where you can pin kernel configs if you want repeatable performance.
[26:18] Priya: For benchmarking, what inputs are best — do you need trace of real traffic or synthetic?
[26:30] Eric: Representative traces are best — we capture sequence length distribution, token arrival patterns, and P95 latency targets. Synthetic tests are useful for stress testing. For the POC we'll want a 10-20 minute sample trace and desired SLOs.
[28:00] Carlos: On failover, if a Dedicated pool goes down, is there automatic fallback to Hosted?
[28:12] Samira: We support automated fallback policies that route to a compatible hosted model variant. Also can do cross-region fallbacks. Fallback adds latency but preserves availability; for strict compliance that prevents cross-tenant routing, you can configure different failover policies.
[30:05] Priya: How long does a model rollout take when you change quantization/profile?
[30:15] Eric: Rollouts are incremental — canaries first, then A/B, then full. For large models with weight conversion it depends on your pool size; typical canaries are minutes, full rollout could be tens of minutes. We keep scoring/eval hooks so you can catch regressions.
[33:40] Ben: Any gotchas with KMS integration? We use HashiCorp Vault and an HSM.
[33:50] Eric: We support external KMS integrations including Vault and cloud KMS. For HSM-backed keys we have an integration path; we'll share the diagram and key rotation policy.
[36:00] Carlos: Do you have examples of customers who've moved from Hosted to Dedicated and what drove it?
[36:10] Samira: Yes — typical drivers: cost predictability, huge concurrency needs, data residency, and stricter SLAs. We'll redact names but provide anonymized case studies.
[38:22] Priya: On autoscaling — does Dedicated autoscale to zero? We want stable baseline to keep caches warm.
[38:35] Eric: Auto-scaling policies are flexible. We support min pool sizes (no scale to zero) to keep KV alive. You can configure burst capacity too.
[40:10] Carlos: What's the billing model for Dedicated? Flat reserved + overage?
[40:18] Samira: Typically reserved monthly commits plus overage at negotiated rates. We'll include cost models in the spreadsheet.
[41:45] Priya: Any measurement of cold vs warm p95 delta for a 4k model?
[42:00] Eric: For a 4k model on H100, warm-path p95 might be ~80-120ms depending on batch target; cold-path can add 50-200ms depending on cache refill. We'll include concrete p50/p95/p99 plots for your traffic shape.
[44:30] Carlos: Would you recommend Dedicated for our use-case? We have sensitive data and expect steady high QPS by Q4.
[44:42] Samira: Based on what you said — yes, Dedicated makes sense: gives VPC isolation, stronger SLAs, pinning for KV, and custom autoscale to preserve cache. We'll size a recommended config.
[46:00] Ben: Next steps recap?
[46:10] Samira: Action items — we'll share perf spreadsheet, security docs, schedule the benchmark, and you provide trace and QPS targets.
[47:30] Carlos: Sounds good. Priya, anything to add?
[47:36] Priya: No, that's it. Thanks.
[48:00] Eric: I'll add notes about kernel selection and quant profiles to the benchmark plan.
[48:12] Samira: Great — thanks everyone. We'll follow up with calendar invites for the benchmark.
[48:30] (meeting ends)
notes: Mentioned ability to pin KV cache on Dedicated
Discussed continuous batching and latency budgets
